newsitem.title: USA: Police seek motorists who grabbed spilled cash.
newsitem.headline: Police seek motorists who grabbed spilled cash.

text.p: Police were searching Wednesday for several motorists who grabbed as much as $250,000 spilled from an armored truck on a suburban interstate highway during rush hour traffic late Tuesday.
One motorist in a white pickup truck may have sped off with more than $20,000, police in Lincoln Park, Michigan, said.

But about $1,500 taken by three people was recovered Wednesday and police were seeking larceny charges against them, said Michigan State Police Lt. Beth Moranty. The felony carries up to a four-year prison term.
"Nobody can be under the impression that this is free money that they just can pick up," Moranty said. "It's not a good commentary on people."
About $250,000 of the $600,000 that fell off the Wolverine Dispatch Inc truck remained missing Wednesday, Moranty said.

The incident started when the truck's driver reported hearing a "whooshing" sound as he drove down Interstate 75 in suburban Lincoln Park. The side door of the truck flew open and two bags of money, containing a total of $600,000, fell out, according to Michigan State Police.

A passing car struck one of the bags, breaking it open and scattering bundles of $20 bills all over the highway. Some motorists stopped to grab money for themselves, while others helped the Wolverine Dispatch guards pick up the spilled cash.
Wolverine Dispatch, based in Comstock Park, Michigan, near Kalamazoo, said it was confident the majority of the funds would be recovered.

"We are investingating the reason for the door malfunction and believe it is related to either an equipment malfunction or a shift of the load hitting the lock release," the company said in a statement.
